what: Harmony Gold mines gold in South Africa, including some of the world's deepest underground mines, and owns a copper and gold project in Papua New Guinea.
customers: Refiners and bullion markets; gold sells at a world price.
money: Hidden Valley in Papua New Guinea and the Wafi-Golpu project
moat: Deep mines with decades of remaining reserves and the specific engineering capability to run them, which almost no company outside South Africa possesses.
risks: South African electricity supply and labour relations are both unreliable
Deep mining is dangerous and costly, and safety stoppages interrupt production
Only three analysts cover the stock
opportunities: 4.9 times earnings and 3.0 times EBITDA with a 29.6% net margin
Revenue grew from $2.6B to $5.7B in four years with the gold price
Analysts see about 65% upside, and $737M of cash against $110M of debt
watch: All-in sustaining cost per ounce and progress on the Wafi-Golpu copper project.
